arxiv-2112-05352.title: Coupling between multiple antennas through a plasma cylinder
arxiv-2112-05352.creator: L. Chang, L. P. Zhang, X. G. Yuan, Y. J. Chang, J. H. Zhang, X. Yang, Y. Wang, H. S. Zhou, G. N. Luo
arxiv-2112-05352.description: Abstract The coupling physics between multiple antennas separated axially along a plasma cylinder is investigated. Experiments are carried out on a recently built device: Physics ANd Thruster oriented HElicon Research (PANTHER), with an upgrade of second-stage antennas. Mutual induction currents are measured in detail.

arxiv-2203-15789.creator: Hao-Ming Fu, Patrick Poirson, Kwot Sin Lee, Chen Wang
arxiv-2203-15789.description: Abstract . Collaborative filtering (CF) is one of the most successful and fundamental techniques in recommendation systems. In recent years, Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based CF models, such as NGCF ( Wang et al. 2019 ) , LightGCN ( He et al. 2020 ) and GTN ( Fan et al. 2021 ) have achieved tremendous success and significantly advanced the state-of-the-art.

arxiv-2206-13214.title: Few-Shot Stance Detection via Target-Aware Prompt Distillation Conference: Proceedings of the 45th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2022; Madrid, Spain. Proceedings of the 45th Int’l ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development
arxiv-2206-13214.creator: Yan Jiang, Jinhua Gao, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng
arxiv-2206-13214.description: Abstract . Stance detection aims to identify whether the author of a text is in favor of, against, or neutral to a given target. The main challenge of this task comes two-fold: few-shot learning resulting from the varying targets and the lack of contextual information of the targets.

arxiv-2208-06900.title: Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks for Intent Detection Based on Anticipatory Brain Potentials Using Electroencephalogram
arxiv-2208-06900.creator: Nathan Lutes, Venkata Sriram Siddhardh Nadendla, K. Krishnamurthy
arxiv-2208-06900.description: Abstract Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are receiving increased attention because they mimic synaptic connections in biological systems and produce spike trains, which can be approximated by binary values for computational efficiency. Recently, the addition of convolutional layers to combine the feature extraction power of convolutional networks with the computational efficiency of SNNs has been introduced.

arxiv-2401-06734.title: On the stability of fractional order Leslie-Gower type model with non-monotone functional response of intermediate predator
arxiv-2401-06734.creator: Shuvojit Mondal, Nandadulal Bairagi
arxiv-2401-06734.description: Abstract In this paper, an attempt is made to understand the dynamics of a fractional order three species Leslie-Gower predator prey food chain model with simplified Holling type IV functional response by considering fractional derivative in Caputo Sense. First, we prove different mathematical results like existence, uniqueness, non-negativity and boundedness of the solutions of fractional order dynamical system.

arxiv-2404-17768.title: Changing the Training Data Distribution to Reduce Simplicity Bias Improves In-distribution Generalization
arxiv-2404-17768.creator: Dang Nguyen, Paymon Haddad, Eric Gan, Baharan Mirzasoleiman
arxiv-2404-17768.description: Abstract Can we modify the training data distribution to encourage the underlying optimization method toward finding solutions with superior generalization performance on in-distribution data? In this work, we approach this question for the first time by comparing the inductive bias of gradient descent (GD) with that of sharpness-aware minimization (SAM).

arxiv-2503-07507.title: PE3R: Perception-Efficient 3D Reconstruction
arxiv-2503-07507.creator: Jie Hu, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang
arxiv-2503-07507.description: Abstract Recent advances in 2D-to-3D perception have enabled the recovery of 3D scene semantics from unposed images. However, prevailing methods often suffer from limited generalization, reliance on per-scene optimization, and semantic inconsistencies across viewpoints. To address these limitations, we introduce PE3R, a tuning-free framework for efficient and generalizable 3D semantic reconstruction.

arxiv-2505-13764.title: Incremental firmware update over-the-air for low-power IoT devices over LoRaWAN
arxiv-2505-13764.creator: Andrea De Simone, Giovanna Turvani, Fabrizio Riente
arxiv-2505-13764.description: Abstract Efficiently supporting remote firmware updates in Internet of Things (IoT) devices remains a significant challenge due to the limitations of many IoT communication protocols, which often make it impractical to transmit full images over low-bandwidth links such as LoRaWAN.

arxiv-2512-15487.title: A plethora of fully localised solitary waves for the full-dispersion Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation Journal: A plethora of solitary waves for FDKP
arxiv-2512-15487.creator: Mats Ehrnström, Mark D. Groves
arxiv-2512-15487.description: Abstract The KP-I equation arises as a weakly nonlinear model equation for gravity-capillary waves with Bond number β > 1 / 3 \beta>1/3 , also called strong surface tension. This equation has recently been shown to have a family of nondegenerate, symmetric ‘fully localised’ or ‘lump’ solitary waves which decay to zero in all spatial directions.

arxiv-2601-12438.title: Revisiting 7 Be Weak and Radiative Transition Rates in Big Bang Nucleosynthesis: Implications for the Primordial Lithium Problem
arxiv-2601-12438.creator: Simone Taioli, Francesca Triggiani, Stefano Simonucci
arxiv-2601-12438.description: Abstract Context. The primordial Li 7 {}^{7}\mathrm{Li} abundance predicted by standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) exceeds the value inferred from old, metal-poor stars by a factor of approximately 3–4. In this model, most primordial 7 Li is produced as 7 Be in the early Universe and subsequently converted by electron capture (EC).

pmc-10607507.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Analysis of the Genes Encoding Q-Type C2H2 Zinc Finger Proteins in Grapevine
pmc-10607507.creator: Mingyu Chu, Tiaoye Wang, Wenfang Li, Yashi Liu, Zhiyuan Bian, Juan Mao, Baihong Chen
pmc-10607507.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Q-type C2H2 zinc finger proteins (ZFPs), the largest family of transcription factors, have been extensively studied in plant genomes. However, the genes encoding this transcription factor family have not been explored in grapevine genomes. Therefore, in this study, we conducted a genome-wide identification of ZFP genes in three species of grapevine, namely Vitis vinifera, Vitis riparia, and Vitis amurensis, based on the sequence databases and phylogenetic and their conserved domains.

pmc-10632194.title: Accumulation of 8-oxodG within the human mitochondrial genome positively associates with transcription
pmc-10632194.creator: Giovanni Scala, Susanna Ambrosio, Margherita Menna, Francesca Gorini, Carmen Caiazza, Marcus S Cooke, Barbara Majello, Stefano Amente
pmc-10632194.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) can be subject to internal and environmental stressors that lead to oxidatively generated damage and the formation of 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2′-deoxyguanine (8-oxodG). The accumulation of 8-oxodG has been linked to degenerative diseases and aging, as well as cancer. Despite the well-described implications of 8-oxodG in mtDNA for mitochondrial function, there have been no reports of mapping of 8-oxodG across the mitochondrial genome. To address this, we used OxiDIP-Seq and mapped 8-oxodG levels in the mitochondrial genome of human MCF10A cells.

pmc-10643965.title: Risk factors and a prognostic model for patients with borderline resectable locally advanced T3–4N0–1 non-small cell lung cancer: a population-based study
pmc-10643965.creator: Yi Liu, Hongjin Lai, Ren Zhang, Liang Xia, Chenglin Guo, Lunxu Liu
pmc-10643965.description: BackgroundNon-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a malignant disease with a significant morbidity rate. For patients diagnosed with borderline resectable locally advanced (T3–4 invasion and N0–1) NSCLC, the optimal treatment and prognosis are still under debate. This study aimed to develop a predictive nomogram that could assess the prognosis of these patients and optimize clinical decision-making.

pmc-11492380.creator: Christopher
pmc-11492380.description: Accurate and complete microkinetic models (MKMs) are powerful for anticipating the behavior of complex chemical systems at different operating conditions. pmc-12528936.title: Sociodemographic heterogeneity in the association between social isolation and all-cause mortality among Japanese older adults: JAGES longitudinal panel study
pmc-12528936.creator: Frances Rom Lunar, Naoki Kondo, Yukiko Honda, Atsushi Nakagomi, Toshiaki Komura, Kosuke Inoue, Koichiro Shiba
pmc-12528936.description: SummaryBackgroundSocial isolation has been linked to higher mortality; however, it remains unknown how this association varies across individuals and social groups.MethodsWe used a nationwide cohort study of ∼20,000 older adults with a 9·4-year follow-up period (Japan Gerontological Evaluation Study, 2013–2022), adjusting for 60 pre-baseline covariates. We also used a national insurance database to ascertain 4299 all-cause deaths.

pmc-13024893.title: Diversity of Mycotoxigenic Penicillium and Associated Mycobiota in Dry-Cured Meat (Cecina, León, Spain) Revealed by a Polyphasic Approach
pmc-13024893.creator: Daniela Cristina Solo de Zaldivar Ribeiro, Alberto Pintor-Cora, Ángel Alegría, Jesús A. Santos, Jose M. Rodríguez-Calleja, Teresa M. López-Díaz
pmc-13024893.description: Cecina de León is a traditional Spanish dry-cured beef product whose surface, as in other similar meat products, becomes heavily colonised by fungi during ripening, raising concerns related to possible mycotoxin contamination. This study aimed to characterise the mycobiota associated with cecina and its production environment, with particular emphasis on mycotoxigenic Penicillium species.

pmc-13389725.title: Challenges in the distribution of community pharmacists in depopulated areas in Japan
